atoms.text: Unfortunately, children’s rights can sometimes be violated, and these violations can be upsetting. If this level upsets you, you should speak with an adult about it.

instruction.text: Read about Maya’s situation. Decide if you think her rights are being violated.

example.a: Maya is 7 years old and works in a clothing factory every day so her family can afford to eat and pay rent. She cannot go to school anymore because she has to spend so much time working.
example.sound: Maya is 7 years old and works in a clothing factory every day so her family can afford to eat and pay rent. She cannot go to school anymore because she has to spend so much time working.

instruction.text: Which two children’s rights are being violated?
Read about Ollie’s situation. Decide if you think his rights are being violated.

example.a: Ollie has to empty the bins once a week and help with the cooking at least twice a week. He finds these jobs really annoying sometimes.
example.sound: Ollie has to empty the bins once a week and help with the cooking at least twice a week. He finds these jobs really annoying sometimes.

instruction.text: Read about Lola’s situation. Decide if you think her rights are being violated.

example.a: Lola loves to play chess. She reads about a chess club for children in the newspaper and asks if she can join the club. The club supervisor replies, “only boys play here. I don’t think you could keep up.”
example.sound: Lola loves to play chess. She reads about a chess club for children in the newspaper and asks if she can join the club. The club supervisor replies, “only boys play here. I don’t think you could keep up.”

instruction.text: Read about Natasha’s situation. Decide if you think her rights are being violated.

example.a: Natasha’s father is often very stressed out by his work. He’s so busy that sometimes he doesn’t have time to take Natasha to the doctors or make her lunch.
example.sound: Natasha’s father is often very stressed out by his work. He’s so busy that sometimes he doesn’t have time to take Natasha to the doctors or make her lunch.

instruction.text: Which two children’s rights are being violated?
Read about Nick’s situation. Decide if you think his rights are being violated.

example.a: Nick is in Year 7 and he would like to go on a camping trip with his friend Lucas in the holidays. In order to save up enough money, he does a short newspaper round every Sunday.
example.sound: Nick is in Year 7 and he would like to go on a camping trip with his friend Lucas in the holidays. In order to save up enough money, he does a short newspaper round every Sunday.
